tasks.short: Run training sessions on site: toolbox talks, onboarding, team lead workshops, role plays, demos on the warehouse floor.

today.trigger: Training calendar in Studytube, a new flex intake, or a team lead asking for a session.
steps: Book room or floor slot around shifts in Outlook
Adapt slides and exercises from the last run
Print attendance list and handouts
Deliver the session in Dutch, often with ad hoc translation for flex workers
Enter attendance in Studytube by hand
drudgery: Rebuilding the same role-play scripts each time
Manual attendance entry
Translating on the spot for Polish and Romanian flex workers
today.time_sinks: Preparation and admin around each session, and repeating the same session per shift and per site.

lenses.faster: AI drafts role-play scenarios, quiz questions and translated handouts from the existing deck; QR check-in replaces paper attendance lists.
lenses.autonomous: Attendance from QR check-in syncs to Studytube after the session without anyone typing it in.
lenses.ambitious: Each team lead gets a practice partner: AI role plays for hard conversations (absence talks under the Wet verbetering poortwachter, safety confrontations) before the live session.
lenses.joy: Less slide fiddling and admin; more time coaching people on the floor, which is what trainers like.
lenses.options: Three variants per session (15-minute toolbox talk, 1-hour workshop, short video) drafted from one source for different shifts.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the session formats and practice scenarios, then trains internal floor trainers to run them.
reach: Coach team leads to run toolbox talks themselves (HR Business Partner work)
Prepare manager briefings on absence conversations with HRBPs

tasks.human_edge: Reading the room, building trust with shift workers, and judging live whether a forklift driver really understands a safety rule.
tasks.pattern_why: The delivery stays human; AI only prepares material, scenarios and practice partners around it.

steps: Copilot drafts scenarios, quiz and handout from the master deck
Translation of handouts into Polish, Romanian and English
Specialist reviews and adjusts
Session delivered live with QR check-in
Attendance syncs to Studytube
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves all content and translations of safety material before use.
data_needed: Glossary of safety terms per language
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube session record and SharePoint content library

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts slides and handouts from existing documents in PowerPoint and Word.
AI chat role plays help managers practise difficult conversations before live training.

risks: Machine translation errors in safety instructions
Role-play scenarios that feel generic or off-culture for warehouse staff
Works council concern if practice conversations are recorded or scored
research_questions: How many hours per month go to preparation versus delivery today, per site?
Do team leads actually use AI role-play practice when offered, and does it change their absence conversations?
Can Studytube accept attendance via QR check-in or API without a paid add-on?

tasks.short: Write and update work instructions, handouts, e-learning and course material, often in several languages.

today.trigger: New process, new equipment, audit finding, or a CAO or legal change.
steps: Collect the SOP or process description from the site manager
Write the instruction or handout in Word or PowerPoint
Get photos from the floor
Have it translated by an agency or a bilingual colleague
Upload to SharePoint and Studytube
drudgery: Reformatting the same content for print, slide and e-learning
Chasing translations
Finding which version of a document is current
today.time_sinks: Writing from scratch, translation turnaround and keeping versions consistent across three sites.

lenses.faster: AI turns an SOP or a recorded floor walkthrough into a B1-level instruction, handout, quiz and short e-learning in one pass, in four languages.
lenses.autonomous: A change to an SOP in SharePoint triggers a draft update of all derived materials and a review task for the owner.
lenses.ambitious: Every warehouse process gets a current, picture-based instruction in the worker's own language, which today exists only for the top processes.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses reformatting and translation chasing; what remains is making the content right and clear.
lenses.options: Several formats from one source: one-page card, 3-minute video, micro-learning, so sites pick what works on their floor.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the content pipeline and style rules (reading level, glossary, version control) instead of writing each document.
reach: Policy summaries for HR Administrator and HRBPs
Onboarding packs the Recruiter sends before day one

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what actually happens on the floor versus the SOP, and judging what a new flex worker will misread.
tasks.pattern_why: Several steps (draft, format, translate, publish) with tools, and safety content needs human approval before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: SOP updated in SharePoint or a content request logged.
steps: Agent drafts instruction, handout and quiz from the SOP and site photos
Applies glossary and B1 reading level
Translates into Polish, Romanian and English
Site expert and specialist approve
Publishes to SharePoint and Studytube with version number
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and the site process owner sign off; safety material also by the safety officer (preventiemedewerker).
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and Studytube course log

evidence.claim: Synthesia generates multilingual training videos from a script.
DeepL translates documents with custom glossaries.
Articulate 360 has an AI assistant that drafts course content and quizzes.

risks: Wrong safety step in a translated instruction leads to an incident
Content drifts from actual floor practice if site experts skip review
Version confusion if old PDFs stay printed on the floor
research_questions: How many SOPs and instructions exist per site, and how many are out of date?
What error rate do translated safety instructions have after AI translation plus glossary, judged by bilingual floor workers?
Does Studytube support importing SCORM or AI-built courses without manual rework?

tasks.short: Organise refresher and skills training: forklift, VCA, food safety, and team lead development, per site.

today.trigger: Certificate about to expire, manager request, or annual training plan.
steps: Export expiring certificates from Studytube to Excel
Match against AFAS employee list and shifts
Email managers to release people
Book external trainer or internal session
Enrol and remind participants
drudgery: Matching Excel lists across Studytube and AFAS
Chasing managers to release staff
Tracking flex worker certificates held by agencies
today.time_sinks: List reconciliation and scheduling around shifts across three sites.

lenses.faster: A rule-based job matches expiring certificates with AFAS rosters and proposes session dates per site.
lenses.autonomous: 90 days before expiry, the worker is auto-enrolled and the manager gets a shift-release request.
lenses.ambitious: Move from compliance refreshers to a skills matrix per role, so people are offered training for the next step (reach truck, team lead) before vacancies open.
lenses.joy: No more Excel matching; the specialist spends time on who should grow, not who is about to lapse.
lenses.options: Per expiring group, scenarios: one central session, per-site sessions, or e-learning plus practical exam, with cost and lost shift hours.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the rules and the skills matrix; the system runs the cycle.
reach: Certificate admin now done by the HR Administrator
Checking flex worker certificates with agencies for the Recruiter and site planners

tasks.human_edge: Deciding who is ready to grow, negotiating time with site managers, and handling people who repeatedly fail.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching is deterministic, but enrolment and manager requests touch several systems and need approval for cost and shifts.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly check on Studytube certificate expiry dates.
steps: Pull expiries and match to AFAS employee and roster data
Propose sessions per site with cost
Specialist approves the batch
Auto-enrol and send manager release requests
Escalate non-responses after 7 days
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves each batch and any external trainer spend.
data_needed: Flex worker certificate data from agencies
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube enrolment log and a Power BI compliance view

evidence.claim: LMS platforms send automatic certificate expiry reminders and re-enrolments.
AFAS Profit and Studytube can be connected via API for employee data.

risks: Wrong roster data causes enrolments on rest days, which costs overtime under the CAO
Flex worker certificates outside Noordhaven's systems stay a gap
Skills matrix seen as performance monitoring by the works council
research_questions: How many certificates lapse per year and what does a lapse cost (idle forklift drivers, audit findings)?
Is there a working Studytube–AFAS integration today, and who owns it?
Will the three agencies share certificate data in a structured way?

tasks.short: Track who did which training and whether it worked: completions, evaluations, incidents, retention.

today.trigger: Month end, an audit, or a question from the HR Director or a site manager.
steps: Export completions from Studytube
Collect evaluation forms and survey results
Combine in Excel with AFAS headcount
Write a short report or slide
Answer follow-up questions by hand
drudgery: Monthly Excel merges
Reading hundreds of free-text evaluation comments
Rebuilding the same report for each site
today.time_sinks: Data merging and summarising open comments; little time left to ask whether training changed anything.

lenses.faster: A Power BI model on Studytube and AFAS data replaces the Excel merge; an LLM groups open comments into themes.
lenses.autonomous: Dashboards refresh nightly and flag sessions with low scores or sites with low completion.
lenses.ambitious: For the first time link training to the North Star: onboarding completed in week one versus 90-day retention, and safety training versus incidents.
lenses.joy: No more copy-paste reports; time goes to asking why a site performs differently.
lenses.options: Compare cohorts (trained vs not, site vs site, e-learning vs classroom) instead of one average score.
lenses.altitude: The specialist defines the measures and questions; the analytics run themselves.
reach: Training sections of reports now built by the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Input to HRBP quarterly reviews with site managers

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a correlation means something, and turning findings into decisions with site managers.
tasks.pattern_why: Data is structured and the metrics can be written down; only free-text comments need an LLM step inside the pipeline.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS and Studytube extract refresh.
steps: Load completions, evaluations and AFAS HR data into Power BI
Run LLM theming on new comments
Compute completion, scores, week-one onboarding and 90-day retention per cohort
Flag outliers to the specialist
Monthly summary drafted for the HR Director
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist checks flagged outliers and the monthly summary before it goes out.
data_needed: Hire date, exit date, site, function from AFAS
Incident data from site safety logs
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI workspace and SharePoint report archive

evidence.claim: Power BI dashboards on HR extracts refreshed nightly are already in place at the company.
LLMs reliably group free-text survey comments into themes.

risks: Linking training data to individuals may count as a personnel monitoring system needing works council consent (WOR art. 27)
AVG/GDPR: purpose limitation and data minimisation for combining training and HR data
Small groups make results traceable to individuals
research_questions: Is there a measurable difference in 90-day retention between hires who complete onboarding in week one and those who do not?
Does the works council see this as a monitoring system requiring consent?
How complete and clean is incident data per site?

tasks.short: Design onboarding and training programmes, for example week-one onboarding for warehouse hires and team lead tracks.

today.trigger: Annual plan, new site process, poor onboarding results, or management request.
steps: Interview site managers and team leads on needs
Draft programme outline in Word
Align with HRBPs, Recruiter and works council where needed
Build schedule and content list
Set up in Studytube
drudgery: Writing outlines from scratch
Turning interview notes into needs lists
Re-planning schedules around shifts
today.time_sinks: Needs gathering and alignment rounds with many stakeholders across three sites.

lenses.faster: AI summarises interview notes into a needs analysis and drafts a programme outline with learning goals, schedule and assessment.
lenses.autonomous: Onboarding tasks per new hire are created automatically from the AFAS start date, per function and site.
lenses.ambitious: A proper week-one onboarding for every flex and permanent hire on every site, which directly feeds the 90-day North Star.
lenses.joy: Less blank-page writing; more time with team leads shaping what new people need.
lenses.options: Three programme designs (lean, standard, extended) with cost, shift impact and expected effect for management to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs programme templates and rules; tailored versions per site and function are generated from them.
reach: Preboarding sequences the Recruiter runs after an offer
Manager onboarding checklists HRBPs now chase

tasks.human_edge: Understanding site politics and culture, getting buy-in from managers and the works council, and choosing what matters.
tasks.pattern_why: Design choices and stakeholder alignment stay with the person; AI speeds up analysis and drafting.

in_practice.trigger: Programme design request or quarterly onboarding review.
steps: Copilot summarises stakeholder notes and existing data
Drafts outline options with cost and schedule
Specialist chooses and adapts with stakeholders
Templates set up in Studytube and onboarding tasks linked to AFAS start dates
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director approve programme; works council consulted where the programme changes working conditions.
data_needed: CAO rules on paid training time

evidence.claim: Copilot in Word and Teams summarises meeting notes and drafts outlines.

risks: Generic programme designs that ignore site differences
Stakeholders bypassed because a draft looks finished
Auto-created onboarding tasks fail when AFAS start dates are late or wrong for flex workers
research_questions: What share of hires completes onboarding in week one today, per site and for flex versus permanent?
Are AFAS start dates for flex workers entered before day one?
Which parts of onboarding do new hires say helped them stay past 90 days?

tasks.short: Compare classroom, e-learning and blended training on cost, effect, lost shift hours and travel between sites.

today.trigger: Budget round, new contract with a training provider, or complaints about a format.
steps: Collect costs from AFAS invoices and provider quotes
Estimate lost hours and travel in Excel
Gather participant feedback
Write a recommendation for the HR Director
drudgery: Pulling invoices and hours together by hand
Building a new spreadsheet each time
today.time_sinks: Data collection on cost and hours; comparisons are rough and rarely repeated.

lenses.faster: A standing cost model per course and mode, fed by AFAS cost data and Studytube completion and score data.
lenses.autonomous: Per course, the model updates each quarter and flags where another mode would be cheaper with equal results.
lenses.ambitious: Every course has a known cost per competent employee per mode, including travel CO2 between Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
lenses.joy: No more one-off spreadsheets; the discussion moves to what works.
lenses.options: Scenarios per course: all classroom, all e-learning, blended, or per-site trainers, with cost, effect and CO2.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets the evaluation criteria and decides; the model does the arithmetic.
reach: Training budget input for the FP&A Analyst
Provider spend analysis now done by the Controller

tasks.human_edge: Judging what a format means for low-literacy or non-Dutch workers, and what can only be learned on a real forklift.
tasks.pattern_why: The cost model is deterministic, but the trade-offs and choice stay a human judgment.

steps: Pull training costs from AFAS and hours from rosters
Join with Studytube results per mode
Generate scenarios with cost, effect and CO2
Specialist drafts recommendation with copilot help
in_practice.human_gate: HR Director approves format changes; budget changes through Finance.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI and the annual training plan on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Power BI can model cost per course combining finance and LMS data.

risks: Cheaper e-learning chosen where practical skill needs hands-on training
Training costs not booked per course in AFAS, so the model rests on estimates
Effect measures too weak to compare modes fairly
research_questions: Are training costs booked per course or provider in the AFAS general ledger?
For forklift and VCA, does blended learning give the same exam pass rate as classroom?
How many paid hours per year go to travel between sites for training?

tasks.short: Keep up with L&D practice, safety rules, certification changes and new learning tools.

today.trigger: Newsletters, conferences, LinkedIn, or a question from management.
steps: Read newsletters and articles
Check VCA, forklift and food-safety scheme updates
Attend webinars
Save notes in OneNote or email folders
drudgery: Skimming a lot of irrelevant content
Checking regulator and scheme sites by hand
today.time_sinks: Volume of reading with little filtered for logistics or the Dutch context.

lenses.faster: A weekly digest filters sources for logistics, Dutch rules and Noordhaven's programmes, with short summaries and links.
lenses.autonomous: Scheme and rule changes (VCA, Arbo, EU AI Act literacy duty under art. 4) are watched and flagged with impact on current courses.
lenses.ambitious: The team shares a running knowledge base of what changed and what it means for each course.
lenses.joy: Less skimming; more time on the few pieces worth reading properly.
lenses.options: Summaries at three depths (headline, one page, full) so the specialist chooses where to go deep.
lenses.altitude: The specialist curates sources and tests what matters; the digest does the scanning.
reach: Briefing HRBPs and the HR Director on legal changes affecting training duties
AI literacy guidance for the whole HR team

tasks.human_edge: Judging which ideas fit Noordhaven's workforce and turning them into practice.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured articles become a structured, sourced digest inside a fixed weekly workflow.

steps: Collect items from chosen sources and scheme sites
LLM filters and summarises with links
Flags items affecting current courses
Specialist reads and logs decisions in SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist verifies any change before it alters a course.
data_needed: List of current courses and certificates

evidence.claim: LLM tools summarise and filter news feeds into digests.
The EU AI Act requires providers and deployers to ensure AI literacy of staff (art. 4), applicable since February 2025.

risks: Summaries miss nuance or misstate a rule change
Filter bubble: only sources already chosen
Paywalled sources not covered
research_questions: Which rule or scheme changes in the past two years were caught late, and what did that cost?
Does the digest cut reading time without missing items the specialists would have flagged?

tasks.short: Review material from internal and external trainers for accuracy, clarity, language level and current procedures.

today.trigger: New or updated material from a trainer or provider.
steps: Read outline, slides and handouts
Check against current SOPs and safety rules
Check language level and readability
Send comments back by email
Re-review the next version
drudgery: Line-by-line checks for outdated procedures
Repeating the same style comments
Tracking review rounds by email
today.time_sinks: Close reading of long decks and several review rounds.

lenses.faster: An LLM checks material against a rubric: SOP consistency, B1 language, glossary, accessibility, and returns tracked comments.
lenses.autonomous: Material uploaded to a SharePoint review folder is checked on arrival and the trainer gets a first comment round automatically.
lenses.ambitious: Every piece of external material is checked before use, not just samples, and providers get a clear quality standard.
lenses.joy: No more repeating style comments; review time goes to substance and safety.
lenses.options: Suggested rewrites in two or three versions for hard passages, so trainers pick one.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the quality rubric and checks the checker's misses.
reach: Quality clauses in provider contracts for the Controller and HR Director

tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether material fits the floor reality and the people, and judging safety-critical content.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured material becomes structured comments against a written rubric; output can be checked.

in_practice.trigger: File uploaded to the SharePoint review folder.
steps: LLM checks against rubric and current SOPs
Returns comments in the document
Specialist reviews and adds substantive points
Comments sent to trainer; approved version published
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves before material is used; safety content also checked by the site safety officer.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint review log with version history

evidence.claim: LLMs review documents against a written checklist and add comments.

risks: False sense of safety if the LLM misses an outdated procedure
Provider material copyright and confidentiality when uploaded
Rubric too strict for practical, visual material
research_questions: How many review rounds does a typical provider deck take today?
In a test on ten past reviews, what share of the specialist's comments does the LLM also find?
Do provider contracts allow uploading their material into Microsoft 365 Copilot?

role.altitude: From building and delivering courses to running Noordhaven's learning system: the skills matrix per role, the certificate compliance engine, the multilingual content pipeline and the measures that link training to 90-day retention.
reach: Certificate and enrolment admin now done by the HR Administrator
Training and onboarding reports for the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Preboarding and onboarding packs for the Recruiter
Manager coaching material and absence-conversation practice with HRBPs
Training budget and provider spend analysis with FP&A and the Controller
AI literacy training for the company under EU AI Act art. 4
role.ceiling_note: Live floor training, practical forklift and VCA exams by certified examiners, works council consultation and site manager buy-in stay human; realistic saving is about 35 to 40% of role time (roughly 550 of 1,600 hours per FTE), mostly in content, admin and reporting.
skills_to_grow: Prompting and reviewing AI-drafted content against a rubric
Power BI and basic data modelling on Studytube and AFAS data
Workflow automation (Power Automate, Studytube and AFAS APIs)
AVG/GDPR and works council rules for learning data
Evaluation design linking training to retention and safety
role.ambitious_version: Every hire, permanent or flex, gets a week-one onboarding in their own language, no certificate ever lapses, and each site sees which training actually keeps people past day 90, with two L&D specialists running it as a system instead of by hand.
